title: Three-Dimensional Acoustic Assembly Device for Mass Manufacturing of Cell Spheroids
protocol: Prepare four 1 mm thick PMMA sheets through laser cutting.
Glue the four PMMA sheets together to form a square chamber with an inner width of 21 mm and a height of 10 mm.
Attach another 1 mm thick PMMA sheet to the bottom of the chamber as a holder for the bioink.

Affix three lead zirconate titanate (PZT) transducers, each measuring 20 mm in length, 10 mm in width, and 0.7 mm in thickness, with a primary resonant frequency of 3 MHz, to the exterior of the three orthogonal walls of the chamber.
Center the bottom PZT transducer beneath the chamber.
Solder wires to the two conductive areas of each PZT transducer.
Secure the device onto a hollow base to prevent the bottom PZT from coming into contact with other countertops.
Mount the acoustic device onto a microscope stage for top-view observation of the chamber's interior.
Position a digital microscope on the side of the device free from PZT transducers for side-view observation of the chamber's interior.
Independently connect the wires from the three PZT transducers in series to three power amplifiers.
Connect each power amplifier to an output channel of function generators.
Program the settings on the function generators for each PZT transducer, specifying parameters such as sinusoidal waveform, frequency, and amplitude.
Fill the chamber of the acoustic device with 75% alcohol for 5 minutes.
Clean the chamber thoroughly with sterile PBS solution.
Irradiate the chamber with UV light in a clean bench for at least 1 hour.
Culture C3A cells in a T25 cell culture flask using DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Wash the bottom of the culture flask twice with PBS when the C3A cells reach approximately 80% confluence.
Add 2 mL of 0.05% trypsin-EDTA to the cell culture flask and incubate at 37 °C.
Stop the trypsinization process by adding 2 mL of complete culture medium.
Transfer the cell solution to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Prepare a 6% (w/v) GelMA solution containing 0.5% (w/v) LAP by dissolving 0.3 g of GelMA and 0.025 g of LAP in 5 mL of phosphate buffer solution (PBS).
Allow the mixture to sit in a 47 °C water bath for 1 hour.
Pass the GelMA solution through a 0.22 µm filter for sterilization.
Resuspend the cell pellet in cell culture medium.
Stain a small volume of cells with a 0.4% trypan blue solution.
Count cells using a clean hemocytometer.
Mix an appropriate amount of C3A cells with the sterilized GelMA solution to prepare bioink at a density of 2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Pre-stain C3A cells by incubating them with 2 µM cell tracker (DiO dye) at 37 °C for 20 min.
Wash the labeled cells with fresh cell culture medium three times before use.
Pipette more than 1 mL of the bioink into a sterilized chamber.
Ensure that the face-to-face distance between the liquid surface and the chamber bottom is an integer multiple of half the acoustic wavelength.
Turn on the function generator and power amplifier to initiate PZT transducer actuation.
Actuate each PZT transducer individually to achieve the optimal parallel-line cellular pattern.
Conduct a frequency sweep near the primary resonant frequency of each PZT transducer.
Simultaneously apply optimal signals to all three PZT transducers to obtain the expected 3D-dot cellular pattern.
Agitate cells evenly in bioink before applying input signals.
Crosslink the bioink using blue light (405 nm, 60 mW/cm², 30 s) to create a 3D hydrogel scaffold.
Carefully transfer the 3D hydrogel scaffold from the chamber into a Petri dish.
Cut the scaffold into small pieces (e.g., 2 mm × 2 mm × 2 mm) using a clean razor.
Add cell culture medium for cultivation.
Observe spheroid formation at different layers of scaffolds using an inverted microscope.
Remove culture medium and thoroughly wash hydrogel scaffolds twice with PBS after 3 days of culture.
Incubate scaffolds with more than 2 mL of GelMA lysis buffer (1: 200 dilution) for 30 min in a cell incubator.
Transfer the solution into a tube.
Centrifuge the solution at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in fresh culture medium.
Assess the viability of cell spheroids using a live/dead staining kit.
Incubate samples with 1 mL of PBS containing 1 µL of Calcein-AM and 2 µL of Propidium Iodide for 15 min at 37 °C.
Wash samples within hydrogel scaffolds directly with PBS twice.
Centrifuge retrieved spheroids at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Wash the spheroid pellet twice before observation.
Observe the samples using a fluorescence microscope and capture images.
Calculate the ratio of Calcein-AM-stained area to the total stained area using ImageJ.
